title: AOM Brand Guidelines v4
summary: Bold Graphic System brand guidelines, built as live React page at /brand/v4.
content:
AOM Brand Guidelines v4: Bold Graphic System

Steffen | 2026-03-09 Comprehensive visual brand guide. Built as a live React page at /brand/v4.

Pinterest DNA

After reviewing 72+ images across the branding, design, art-direction, typography, grids, and AOM boards, the patterns are clear:

What Patrik gravitates toward:

  • Nike's graphic confidence (Makers of the Game, VaporMax, Harlem Division None). Bold condensed type in grid boxes. B&W photos with type wrapping around them. Patterns as brand elements (VaporMax repeating shapes along the right edge).
  • Industrial data aesthetics (DesignMart barcode labels, marker brand labels). Dense information structured into grids. Every piece of data has a place. This is the badge/pill system at full expression.
  • Circulus poster energy. Black backgrounds, orange accent, photography punching through. Classic European graphic design meets streetwear confidence.
  • AIR UK brand. Orange on black, all caps, mobile-first presentation. Direct ancestor of AOM's color system.
  • UGC Portfolio template. Alternating black/cream sections, huge stats as visual anchors, data grids, bold headers. This is the exact layout language for brand guidelines.
  • Golf Wang / Tyler the Creator. Saturated color moments, personality, real human energy. The antidote to corporate.
  • Basketball court diagrams. Technical precision as aesthetic. Grid lines, measurements, annotations. The "blueprint" quality.

The core insight: AOM's brand guidelines should look like a Nike campaign book crossed with an industrial technical manual. Alternating dark/light sections. Huge section numbers. Orange pattern strips as dividers. Data as visual design.

What's New in v4 (vs previous guidelines)

  1. Pattern Library (the missing piece Patrik called out)

    • Diagonal Lines: 45-degree repeating lines for section dividers and card accents
    • Dot Grid: Radial dot pattern for subtle background texture
    • Cross Hatch: Industrial texture overlay for editorial and blueprint feel
    • Angular Grid: Technical drawing aesthetic with grid + diagonal + centered squares
    • Film Grain: SVG noise filter for video overlays and cinematic photo treatment
    • Orange Bar Stack: Rhythmic stacked bars for data visualization accents
    • Pattern Strip: Full-width pattern divider between sections (used throughout the guidelines themselves)

  2. Dark Frame Color System (evolved from v2 proposal)

    • Night (#0C0C0C) as primary dark surface (65% of page)
    • Night Card (#151515) for elevated surfaces on dark
    • Text Light (#F0ECE6) warm white, never cold blue
    • Text Light Muted (#8A847C) for secondary text on dark
    • Orange Glow (rgba(232,93,38,0.15)) for accent shadows and hover states
    • Full contrast ratio table with AA pass/fail ratings

  3. Visual Typography Specimens

    • Syne display specimen with H1-H4 scale rendered live
    • Space Grotesk body specimen with body/small/label/micro rendered live
    • Complete type scale table with font, size, weight, line height, tracking

  4. Component Library (styled, not just described)

    • Buttons: Primary (orange + glow shadow), Secondary (ghost border), Ghost (text + arrow), Small, Sage variant
    • Badges: Default, Orange, Sage, Gold, Filled, Glow, On-Light variants
    • Cards: Dark, Frosted (backdrop-blur), Orange Accent (glow border), Light
    • Dividers: Orange bar, subtle border, pattern strip, gradient glow line

  5. Photography Style Guide

    • Dramatic lighting rules (always a clear light source)
    • Zero stock tolerance
    • Cropping rules with specific aspect ratios (16:9, 4:5, 1:1, 3:4)
    • Photo treatment specs (border weights by section, film grain opacity)
    • Color grade direction (warm, slightly desaturated, rich blacks)
    • People photography (candid over posed, action over smiling)

  6. Voice & Tone with Do/Don't Examples

    • Confident: "We deliver in days, not weeks." vs "We strive to meet our delivery targets."
    • Human: "Small team. Big output. No layers." vs "Our streamlined organizational structure..."
    • Alive: "Impossible to ignore." vs "High-quality content solutions."
    • 8 numbered copy rules

  7. Spacing & Grid System

    • 12-column grid visualized with column indicators
    • Complete spacing scale: 4px to 96px with named sizes and use cases
    • Section spacing rules with clamp values

Pattern CSS Recipes

Diagonal Lines

background: repeating-linear-gradient(
  45deg,
  transparent,
  transparent 5px,
  rgba(232,93,38,0.08) 5px,
  rgba(232,93,38,0.08) 6px
);

Dot Grid

background: radial-gradient(
  circle,
  #E85D26 1px,
  transparent 1px
);
background-size: 20px 20px;

Cross Hatch

background:
  repeating-linear-gradient(
    45deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.03) 0px,
    rgba(255,255,255,0.03) 1px,
    transparent 1px, transparent 8px
  ),
  repeating-linear-gradient(
    -45deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.03) 0px,
    rgba(255,255,255,0.03) 1px,
    transparent 1px, transparent 8px
  );

Film Grain (SVG)

<svg>
  <filter id="grain">
    <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.85" numOctaves="4" stitchTiles="stitch" />
    <feColorMatrix type="saturate" values="0" />
  </filter>
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" filter="url(#grain)" opacity="0.15" />
</svg>

Section Contrast Pattern

Dark  -> Pattern Strip -> Light -> Pattern Strip -> Dark -> Pattern Strip -> Light -> ...

The alternating dark/light sections with orange pattern strip dividers is the core visual rhythm. This is directly inspired by the UGC Portfolio pin layout and Nike's campaign book approach.

Live Page

Built at: /brand/v4 in the aom-studio repo. File: src/pages/BrandGuidelinesV4.jsx Route added in src/main.jsx

This is a standalone page. Bobby can reference it as the source of truth for all brand decisions. Patterns, colors, components, type, photography rules, voice guidelines are all in one visual document.
